Subject: Capacity heatcheck + OKR sync: QBR prep

Team —

We're a month out from the QBR and I want a concise heatcheck on the infra capacity and unit-econ items I'll be briefing leadership on. High level ask: can each of you surface the one slide/metric we should show for the QBR (focused on GPU spend, utilization, and the measurable impact of batching/caching)? Please keep it short.

Specifics I need by EOD Fri (2026-08-13):
- Current committed GPU capacity vs on-demand buffer (p50/p95)
- Trailing 90-day utilization (GPU occupancy by model class) and any anomalies
- Short-run mitigation levers (batching configs, KV cache hit rate, quantization profiles) and expected % cost delta
- Any open asks that need exec approval (credits, extra reserve, marketplace credits)

I'll synthesize into a single 2-slide QBR artifact for ops/finance. Attach any data tables to your reply.

Thanks —
Connor

Connor —

Attaching the capacity model (capacity_model_v3.xlsx) and a 1-page summary below for slide-ready notes. TL;DR: we have ~12% spare committed capacity at steady state; p95 demand spikes cross that buffer 2–3 hours/day (UTC peak).

Slide bullet suggestions (for leadership):
- Committed vs demand: 120 committed GPUs (reserve pools) vs peak demand equivalent ~135 GPUs (p95 spike) — "buffer shortfall = ~15 GPUs (~12% of steady-state commit)"
- Utilization: 68% avg across batches; inference-heavy models at 82% during peak windows
- Financial impact: current overage (on-demand) for last 30 days = $42k; with conservative batching we project reducing on-demand spend by ~25% => $10.5k/mo savings

Open asks for exec signoff:
1) Option to top up committed pool by +20 GPUs for two months (forecast cost delta ~ $75k/mo vs current on-demand delta) — recommended during product launch windows.
2) Formal approval to enable aggressive KV prefix caching for customer pools (requires a short SOC/data-review doc) — reduces per-token work for repeated prompts.

Notes on methodology: numbers in spreadsheet include model-class splits, bucketed seq-len distributions, and a quick sensitivity table for batching window sizes (4ms, 8ms, 16ms).

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP Product — Console & Observability

Connor / team —

Uploading the batching sims (batching_sim_results.pdf) and calling out the most material finding: moving from our conservative 8ms batching window to a 12ms window increases average batch size by ~18% for short sequence workloads, improving throughput and lowering per-token cost by ~9% in sims. Caveats: tail latency increases for single-token requests; we can mitigate via a hybrid policy (latency-sensitive route + batch route).

Numbers snapshot (last 30d):
- Avg tokens/day: 1.2B
- Cost per million tokens (current): $15.2 (infra-only)
- Projected cost per million tokens w/ 12ms batch: $13.8 (infra-only)
- Estimated change to GPU utilization: +5–7% on batchable models

Actionable ask: If leadership is comfortable with a modest tail-latency SLA delta for low-priority routes, we recommend enabling a staged 12ms policy for non-interactive workloads by next week.

-Marissa
Sr Manager, Inference Performance
Redwood Inference

Folks —

Quick scenario addendum for the slide deck: I ran a 3-scenario run for commit sizing in the spreadsheet (conservative / balanced / opportunistic). Key lines to call out for leadership:
- Conservative: hold current commit, pay on-demand for spikes — protects cash but yields ~$420k/yr on-demand premium
- Balanced (recommended): +15 GPUs committed with auto-burst policy (holds costs to ~$120k/yr premium vs conservative but reduces p95 latency incidents by >60%)
- Opportunistic: +40 GPU commit runs into higher fixed cost but reduces variable spend to near-zero and supports sustained growth for feature launches (~$650k/yr fixed incremental)

Also: adding a short appendix row that quantifies KV cache hit-rate improvements from 0.38 to 0.62 (with the proposed prefix caching change) gives an effective per-token compute reduction of ~18% for repeat-heavy workloads — worth calling out as a durable lever.

Related link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/qbr-2026-infra (has the three scenario tabs).

If we decide on the Balanced path I can draft the procurement ask and term sheet for the commit top-up.

- Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
